workarounds.symptom: [Bug]: Batch-planning CLI backend fails the package UTF-8 guard and decodes receipts with the host locale
workarounds.workaround: Fix: fix(planning): read the batch-planning CLI as UTF-8. Target files: benchmark/runtime/planning.py, loopx/control_plane/goals/planning_batch.py, tests/control_plane/test_benchmark_planning_batch.py. On a non-UTF-8 host, the batch-planning entry reads both of its wrapped-CLI JSON payloads with the host locale codec. `CliPlanningBatchBackend._call` decoded the write receipt with `locale.getpreferredencoding(False)`; `task_plan_packet` decoded the initial `todo plan` packet the same way. `apply_initial_plan` reads that packet... (Ref: https://github.com/loopx-project/loopx/pull/9400)

workarounds.symptom: [Bug]: static presentation packaging certifies text assets outside its eight-suffix allow-list without scanning them
workarounds.workaround: Fix: fix(presentation): scan every static-site text asset and fail closed on unreviewable text. Target files: loopx/presentation/static_site.py, tests/test_static_site_presentation.py. `loopx presentation package` certifies a whole static-site bundle as public-safe while inspecting only eight filename suffixes and decoding only UTF-8, so ordinary text assets such as `.csv` chart data, `.log` captures, `.yaml` config, `.env`, `Dockerfile`, `.map`/`.tsbuildinfo` JSON and BOM-marked or BOM-less UTF-16 captures are copied into th... (Ref: https://github.com/loopx-project/loopx/pull/9406)

workarounds.symptom: [Bug]: static presentation packaging certifies text assets above 2 MB without scanning them
workarounds.workaround: Fix: fix(presentation): scan every static-site text asset at the public boundary. Target files: loopx/presentation/static_site.py, tests/test_static_site_presentation.py. Static-site publication can currently be certified public-safe while a text asset in the scanner's supported suffix set is larger than 2 MB and carries an unscanned provider token; this PR removes the size exemption for those supported text assets. (Ref: https://github.com/loopx-project/loopx/pull/9370)

workarounds.symptom: [Bug]: Release tag verification fails the package UTF-8 guard and reds the required pytest lane
workarounds.workaround: Fix: fix(release): pin UTF-8 on release tag verification. Target files: loopx/control_plane/testing/release_evaluation_gate.py. Latest `main` fails its package-wide text-mode UTF-8 guard, so every pull request that triggers the Python test lane inherits a red `pytest` and `merge-gate`; the same release-qualification call decodes Git output with the host locale on non-UTF-8 Windows hosts. (Ref: https://github.com/loopx-project/loopx/pull/9366)

workarounds.symptom: [Bug]: Windows: portfolio real-tool scenario fails — node:sqlite cannot open the 267-char authority path (MAX_PATH); a second host-dependent layer behind it
workarounds.workaround: Fix: fix(sqlite_authority_store): surface underlying SQLite error in status. Target files: loopx/control_plane/coordination/sqlite_authority_store.ts. The issue was that SQLite errors (like "unable to open database file" due to path length limits on Windows) were being collapsed into a generic "lock contention" message in the `readFailure` function. This made it difficult to diagnose the root cause of database opening failures. (Ref: https://github.com/loopx-project/loopx/pull/8459)

workarounds.symptom: [Bug]: Host recovery I/O uses the locale codec, silently dropping non-ASCII Antigravity Stop events on cp936
workarounds.workaround: Fix: fix(runtime): pin UTF-8 on host recovery I/O. Target files: loopx/agy_goal_mode/host_runtime.py, loopx/hosts/managed_service_runtime.py, tests/test_antigravity_host_runtime.py. Latest `main` fails its two package-wide UTF-8 guards, so every pull request inherits a red Python test lane; the same omissions silently discard non-ASCII Antigravity Stop recovery on cp936 Windows and can block managed-runtime journal recovery. (Ref: https://github.com/loopx-project/loopx/pull/8031)

workarounds.symptom: [Bug]: native Windows Codex App settlement plans emit a POSIX-only Turn reference
workarounds.workaround: Fix: fix(quota): render host-native settlement Turn references. Target files: loopx/control_plane/quota/effect_program.py, tests/control_plane/test_quota_settlement.py. Native Windows Codex App admission can block every no-Turn settlement after the work succeeds because the returned plan contains a POSIX-only Turn placeholder that PowerShell forwards as an empty argument; this affects the supported native Windows App journey and the validation, writeback, spend, and closeout steps generated from it. (Ref: https://github.com/loopx-project/loopx/pull/7823)
